uk-scotland.title: Flag of Scotland (St Andrew's Cross)

colors.note: The Saltire (Cross of St Andrew), Scotland's patron saint.

desc:
- The Saltire (St Andrew's Cross) is a white diagonal cross on blue
- Dating to the 9th century, it may be the oldest flag in continuous use in the world after the Dannebrog
- **Construction:** a blue (royal blue or sky blue) field bearing a white saltire (St Andrew's Cross) extending to all four corners
trivia:
- Scotland uses St. Andrew's Cross (the saltire) as its national flag
- The white cross on blue represents St. Andrew, patron saint of Scotland
- One of the oldest national flags still in use

uk-wales.title: Flag of Wales (Y Ddraig Goch)

colors.note: The leek and the green fields of Wales.
The red dragon (Y Ddraig Goch), symbol of Wales since the Roman period.

desc: - The Welsh flag features a red dragon (Y Ddraig Goch) on a white-over-green field. Notably, Wales is not represented in the Union Jack
- **Construction:** two equal horizontal bands of white (top) and green (bottom), with a large red dragon (Y Ddraig Goch) passant centred on the flag
trivia:
- The red dragon on the Welsh flag does not appear in the Union Jack because Wales was already annexed to England when the Union Flag was created
- The dragon (Y Ddraig Goch) has been a Welsh symbol since medieval times
- The green and white represent the colours of Wales's traditional heraldry

uk-england.title: Flag of England (St George's Cross)

colors.note: The Cross of St George, patron saint of England since the 13th century.

desc:
- The St George's Cross is a red cross on a white field, used since the medieval period. It forms the dominant element of the Union Jack
- **Construction:** a white field with a red St George's Cross
- The cross arms are approximately one-fifth of the flag's dimensions in width, extending to all edges
trivia:
- England uses St. George's Cross as its national flag
- The red cross on white represents St. George, the patron saint of England
- One of the oldest national symbols in the world

uk-northern-ireland.title: Ulster Banner

colors.note: The Red Hand of Ulster and the Cross of St George.

desc:
- The Ulster Banner (1953–1972) was the official flag of Northern Ireland
- It features the Red Hand of Ulster, a six-pointed star, and a crown on a red cross
- **Construction:** (unofficial) a white field with a red St George's Cross bearing the Red Hand of Ulster on a white six-pointed star, crowned
trivia:
- Northern Ireland uses a specific flag representing the region's identity
- Reflects the complex political status and cultural divisions
- Official flag status remains contested between different communities

uk-cornwall.title: Flag of Cornwall (St Piran)

colors.note: The Cornish tin miners and Celtic heritage.
The Cross of St Piran, patron saint of Cornwall.

desc: - St Piran's flag — a white cross on black — represents Cornwall. Legend says it symbolises white tin flowing from black ore
- **Construction:** a black field with a white cross (St Piran's Cross). The cross arms extend to all four edges
trivia:
- Cornwall has its own distinct flag representing the Cornish people
- The black and white represent traditional Cornish identity
- Cornwall maintains a distinct cultural and linguistic heritage
